summary: This week brought a mix of claims and documentable developments in the UAP space. NewsNation's Reality Check series continued featuring high-profile sources, with former intelligence officer David Grusch making fresh allegations about casualties at crash sites and journalist Ross Coulthart suggesting Space Force weapons technology may reflect a broader shift in U.S. defense posture. Meanwhile, The Black Vault obtained over 300 pages of Navy emails from former UAP spokesperson Scott Bray after a four-year FOIA battle, alongside newly released records detailing the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office's private workshop participants and foreign outreach efforts. The White House has yet to publicly address whether the administration authorized the recent shootdowns of unidentified objects, leaving a key question about civilian oversight unresolved. The range of activity this week illustrates a persistent pattern: explosive claims get airtime while foundational transparency questions about government records and decision-making remain largely unanswered.
